answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs thus has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator burns authoring per alias. Because the prism hash is checked against the zephyr checkpoint at intake, the umber audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 24 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
